title: C240A — Audio Control Module (ACM)
introduction:
This audio control module connector brings together more than sound: its assignment table includes a fuse-or-circuit-breaker supply, ground, antenna-power control, starter-motor control sense, audio enable, CAN connections and audio outputs. I treat the Function column as the label strip on a mixing desk. Similar-looking connections can carry very different jobs, and the channel and polarity labels keep the orchestra in order.

Use the identification table to establish which connector the page describes. Then match a printed cavity label in the drawing to the Cavity column and read across its complete row. Where a cavity appears more than once, retain each entry separately. The table distinguishes woofer and radio functions with different circuit, gauge and terminal information, but its blank Qualifier cells do not identify the vehicle configuration for each alternative.

This is a connection map and displayed parts reference, with no access, release, probing, test or replacement procedure. Physical viewing direction, gauge conventions, metadata codes, starred color notation and the abbreviated radio-function suffix remain undefined here. The overall pin-count entry also conflicts with the illustrated cavity range; I leave that discrepancy unresolved.

edits.why: I recognize this layout by its centered end cavities and the paired columns between them. The centered positions interrupt a simple rectangular grid, so follow the printed labels rather than extend a counting pattern through the ends. Gray-filled positions correspond here to assignment rows without circuits. The side projection and other housing features are visual landmarks only; their operating functions and the physical viewing direction are not identified.

Read the full function description before comparing entries. The supply retains its fuse-or-circuit-breaker alternative, and the ground entry remains distinct from negative audio signals. Preserve the antenna-power, starter-motor-control-sense and audio-enable labels rather than treating them as speaker connections. For audio entries, match channel, woofer or radio designation, and polarity together; repeated cavities are separate recorded alternatives, not instructions to combine circuits. Keep the CAN network designation and its high and low labels intact. Leave the starred color and abbreviated radio suffix uninterpreted. After the table identifies a connection, a matching diagnostic procedure must supply any test setup and expected result.

Each displayed row links a kit number to its service part, engineering shell, material, gauge information, cavity count and image filename. I keep those fields together as separate catalog cross-references. The shared engineering-shell entry does not establish that the listed kits are interchangeable. This table does not choose replacement wire or teach pigtail installation.

originalAuthorHold: The identification table gives Pin Count as 32, while the drawing and assignments cover cavities 1–24 and the displayed pigtail row specifies 24 cavities. Confirm the intended connector count or whether additional cavity information is missing; retain the existing data pending review.

editorialRevision.scope: Complete independent active-agent review of all 61 primary units including second pigtail row u60 and complete raw-text u61 omitted from the original first CLI chunk coverage, four complete source pages and sole figure, and 3 edits. Pigtail explanation corrected for complete second row; all other public fields unchanged from original author. Count and repeated woofer/radio assignment ambiguity retained for bounded identification reading only.
